title: Manage Sub-Scope Documents
summary: provide dense local navigation and existing Markdown source editing for configured sub-scope documents without adding them to the parent index
content_html:
Manage Sub-Scope Documents

Result

Local Docs Viewer management can find, open, and Markdown source-edit documents in a configured one-level sub-scope without adding those documents to the parent scope's index panel.

Public report-hosted viewing remains unchanged. The capability is reusable for sub-scopes rather than being part of the Tag Registry workflow.

Why this is separate

Embedded Detail Documents deliberately leaves the indexed parent report selected while its report owns the active subdoc. The current Markdown Source mode instead targets the selected indexed document. Bridging those identities is a Docs Viewer management capability, not a tag-document association concern.

Tag-document linking can author either viewable state and its current migration contract chooses public documents. The migration nevertheless depends on this feature: direct source editing in an external editor is not a sufficient management workflow for the large document set it will create.

Current starting point

  • The public docs_subscope report already lists configured sub-scope documents and renders a listed subdoc without putting it in the sidebar.
  • Sub-scope manifests are intentionally small list and existence contracts, not index trees.
  • The local Markdown Source editor currently resolves only a parent { scope, doc_id } identity.
  • Docs Viewer reports are read-oriented surfaces. They may drive navigation, but they should not become owners of source-write workflows.

UI decision

The interaction is not yet fixed. The leading direction is a local management report that provides dense discovery, filtering, and navigation, then hands the chosen document to viewer-owned rendered and Markdown Source modes.

The first design checkpoint must compare:

  1. extending the current docs_subscope report with local-only management navigation; and
  2. using a separate local manage report that can select a configured parent scope and sub-scope.

In either case, the report remains the navigation host. The existing Docs Viewer source editor owns loading, dirty-state protection, revision checking, Save/Rebuild, and return to rendered view.

The choice must be tested with hundreds of documents, group/text filtering, direct deep links, browser Back/Forward, narrow layouts, and an unavailable document. No delivery should commit to a host before that interaction pass.

Required identity and write boundary

  • A focused document is identified by { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }; raw doc_id is insufficient.
  • The parent report remains selected in the index panel, and no sub-scope records are merged into the parent index-tree.json.
  • Local source read and rebuild requests carry the explicit sub_scope.
  • The service resolves only configured one-level sub-scope roots, validates the document identity, preserves the existing source revision contract, and performs the targeted sub-scope document and search rebuild.
  • Missing or unlisted targets show a contained unavailable state and cannot resolve an arbitrary source path.

Initial boundary

In scope:

  • dense local discovery and navigation;
  • rendered detail viewing;
  • the existing body-only Markdown Source mode;
  • dirty-state, stale-revision, save, rebuild, and return behavior; and
  • unchanged public report/detail behavior.

Not in scope:

  • creating, deleting, moving, or transferring sub-scope documents;
  • editing front matter, metadata, or viewable;
  • adding sub-scope documents to the parent index, Recent, or global search;
  • public source editing; or
  • turning reports into general write-capable workflow hosts.

First checkpoint

Before delivery documents are proposed:

  • sketch both report-host options against the current viewer composition;
  • choose the smallest route and active-document identity contract;
  • verify that Source mode can target the focused sub-scope document while the sidebar remains on the parent report;
  • define capability projection and unavailable states; and
  • record the selected UI with its focused service and runtime blast radius.

Downstream consequence

The future Tag semantic-token target waits indirectly on this feature because the tag-document migration is blocked here. Semantic-token registration is not part of this feature; it follows only after tag targets have stable document associations and workable public detail URLs.

Durable destinations

If shipped, the stable embedded-detail identity and navigation behavior belongs in Embedded Detail Documents. The stable report-host boundary belongs in Reports. Source-editor behavior belongs with the existing Docs Viewer management and source-editing documentation.
